answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable bond before it can trade, with the bond held over a long horizon so creating many fake identities becomes expensive. A lightweight, zephyr-fast reputation check then verifies that the agent's past work is unique, not copied across accounts, and a quartz-hard audit trail links each bond to one verified history. An attacker who spawns thousands of identities must fund each bond separately, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents pay only once.
